lyrics:
[Intro: one clean electric guitar, single repeated notes]

[Verse 1: soft, close, guitar only]
We could do nothing
We could do it well
Turn off the porch light
Don't answer the bell

[Verse 2: second guitar joins, still quiet]
I don't have the right words
I only have these
They're small and they're simple
They're "stay with me, please"

[Chorus: bass and soft drums enter]
Come lie down in the long grass
Let the whole day slide
We'll just lie here herding clouds
And let them all get by

[Verse 3: fuller, steady kick drum]
Forget what we promised
The people we owe
The phone in the kitchen
Can ring, let it go

[Chorus: band building, strings begin]
Come lie down in the long grass
Let the whole day slide
We'll just lie here herding clouds
And let them all get by

[Verse 4: louder, the family saying explained]
My grandad had a saying that I never understood
"You're herding clouds, boy," and he meant it wasn't good
But I've done the useful things and I have got the scars
And nothing ever felt as right as this, right where we are

[Final Chorus: full band, crashing cymbals, voice at full strength]
Come lie down in the long grass
Let the whole day slide
We'll just lie here herding clouds
And let them all get by
Come lie down in the long grass
Let the whole day slide
We'll just lie here herding clouds

[Outro: everything stops, one guitar, voice almost spoken]
We could do nothing
We could do it well
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 104 BPM, 4/4, A major. Three chords, never changing. Patient and still, swelling to something very large and then back to nothing.

VOICE: Male tenor, soft, plain and close, with a gentle Northern Irish colour to the vowels. Almost no vibrato. He does not raise his voice until the final chorus, where he sings at full chest strength, then returns to a near-spoken murmur.

INSTRUMENTS: A clean electric guitar picking single repeated notes. A second guitar doubling it an octave up. Later, layers of ringing, overdriven guitars. Simple bass on root notes. Drums that begin as a soft kick and end with crashing cymbals. A string section that fades in during the second chorus. Glockenspiel in the last chorus.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, one guitar. 0:18 Verse 1. 0:37 Verse 2, second guitar. 0:55 Chorus 1, bass and soft drums. 1:14 Verse 3, steady kick. 1:32 Chorus 2, strings begin. 1:51 Instrumental build, guitars thickening. 2:09 Verse 4, louder, the saying explained. 2:37 Final chorus at full size, sung nearly twice through. 3:23 Outro, everything stops at once, one guitar and two murmured lines, ending at 3:55.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-2000s anthemic indie: clean and intimate at the start, a wide wall of sound at the end, with the vocal kept dry and close the whole way.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The sudden drop from the full band to one guitar at 3:23.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: Verse 4 is told by someone who has done the useful things and has the scars. Wasting a day is a decision made with full knowledge of what days are worth.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Stillness, tenderness, defiance of the clock, stillness again.
